title: Ube Halaya: Moulded Purple Yam Jam with Coconut Milk
summary: Grated purple yam slowly cooked with coconut milk, evaporated milk, sugar and butter until thick and glossy, then set in a mould and turned out.
equipment: large non-stick or heavy saucepan or wok
600 ml fluted jelly mould or bowl

ingredients.item: unsalted butter, plus a little for the mould
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Dry the ube
steps.text: Cook the grated ube in the pan over medium-high heat for 3-4 min, stirring, until any excess water has evaporated and the colour deepens. Starting dry means less time stirring later.

steps.title: Add the milks
steps.text: Stir in the coconut milk, evaporated milk and sugar and bring to the boil. Turn down to a gentle simmer so it bubbles lazily rather than spits.

steps.title: Stir patiently
steps.text: Cook for about 30 min, scraping the base and corners every minute or so with the spatula, until thick and jammy. Constant scraping stops the milk sugars catching and scorching.

steps.title: Enrich with butter
steps.text: Add the 50 g butter and the salt and keep stirring over low heat for 10-15 min more. It is ready when deep violet and glossy and it pulls away from the pan as one mass.

steps.title: Pack the mould
steps.text: Butter the mould generously and pack in the hot halaya. Tap the mould firmly on the worktop to knock out air pockets, then smooth the base.

steps.title: Chill and turn out
steps.text: Cool, cover and chill for at least 3 h so it firms enough to hold its shape. Run a thin knife around the edge, turn out onto the plate and cut into slices or wedges.

tips: A common mistake is stopping too early: if it does not leave the pan clean, it will not hold its shape.
Use a heavy pan and a silicone spatula to reach every corner.
Thaw frozen ube completely and squeeze out any extra liquid before you start.
Spoon leftovers over halo-halo or spread on toast.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 1 week, or freeze in portions for up to 2 months and thaw overnight in the fridge.
